newsitem.title: FRANCE: Roadblocks melting all over France - officials.
newsitem.headline: Roadblocks melting all over France - officials.

text.p: Roadblocks were melting away all over France on Friday afternoon after truck drivers' unions ended talks with employers reporting substantial progress on pay and working hours, the national road traffice centre said.

By 4 p.m. (1500 GMT) there were 190 roadblocks left compared to 249 at the peak on Thursday, and officials reported drivers were starting to lift many of the remaining blockades at oil refineries, fuel depots and borders.

The barricades began to come down rapidly after trade union leaders ended talks with employers reporting substantial progress on the key issues of pay and work time and saying they would consult strikers on ending the 12-day blockade.
"Many of the blockades are just melting away," an official at the traffic information centre said.

Blockades were lifted in the biggest Channel port of Calais, at the borders with Germany and Italy, on the Seine river bridges near Le Havre, at the Elf oil refinery at Donges, near Saint-Nazaire and around the towns of Chateauroux, Avignon and Arles.

Petrol rationing remained in force in almost half of the country after more than a third of the 18,000 petrol stations ran out of fuel. The strike has disrupted industry in France and had economic side-effects in all neighbouring countries.
